messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Computation of pseudo-R squared logit models using INLA
parts:
On Mon, 2016-06-13 at 03:03 -0700, K.e wrote:
> Thanks. 
> Pseudo R squared are R squared calculated for  the logistic models.
> http://thestatsgeek.com/2014/02/08/r-squared-in-logistic-regression/
>

The McFadden's pseudo-R squared, can be computed manually, using two
runs, like

> n = 10; y = rnorm(n); x = rnorm(n); r = inla(y ~ 1 + x, data =
data.frame(y,x), control.compute = list(dic=TRUE))
> r0 = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y,x), control.compute =
list(dic=TRUE))
> r$dic$deviance.mean
[1] 27.16944354
> r0$dic$deviance.mean
[1] 29.15843203
> 1 - r$dic$deviance.mean/r0$dic$deviance.mean
[1] 0.06821314949



or if you want to use the 'mean deviance' instead, its there is the dic
object.
